PullRequest.Title: agent bakeoff
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/335085 Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/9405 Adds `sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled` off by default ## Summary - add **Run Multiple Agents...** to the agent picker behind the off-by-default `sessions.chat.compareAgents.enabled` experiment - configure independent attempts with provider-local agents and models, including repeated agent/model combinations with stable attempt IDs - preserve setup selections while the picker is dismissed and clear them only after a successful submission - launch attempts directly in isolated worktrees, then run a visible Judge after the attempts finish - require the Judge to review every diff, inspect available evidence, and run missing targeted validation without modifying attempts - record privacy-safe telemetry for attempt duration, the models used, and the model selected by the Judge; correlate provider-native OTel spans for token analysis - present a recommendation-first comparison result with explicit review, synthesis, and cleanup actions ## UX 1. Select **Run Multiple Agents...** in the agent picker. 2. Add or remove attempt rows and choose an agent and provider-local model for each attempt. 3. Optionally expand **Evaluation** to choose the Judge agent and model. 4. Select **Run N Attempts**. Each attempt runs in parallel in its own isolated worktree. 5. The comparison parent summarizes progress and becomes `Comparison · Review ready` when the Judge submits a verdict. 6. The Judge result leads with the recommended attempt and rationale. A collapsed **Attempt time and token usage** disclosure shows each attempt's elapsed time and provider-reported input-plus-output tokens. 7. Select **Focus Winning Session** to open the recommended attempt, or use its dropdown to focus another attempt. Selecting the comparison group header opens all available attempts in a tiled grid. The prompt and attached context are frozen when the comparison launches. Judge recommendations remain advisory. Synthesis and worktree cleanup are always explicit, and no attempt is automatically applied or deleted. ## Reviewer notes Comparison records are provider-neutral and persisted in profile storage. Setup is represented as an array of uniquely identified attempts rather than a map keyed by harness, allowing different models from one harness or repeated runs of the same configuration. Model identifiers remain provider-local and the UI displays provider-owned model labels. There is intentionally no equivalent-model-across-providers behavior. Attempts, the Judge, and explicit synthesis are ordinary sibling sessions in one comparison group. The Judge is the automatic machine-review stage; **Review Recommended Attempt** is the explicit human verification stage. New verdicts distinguish attempt-reported validation, Judge-run validation, and unavailable evidence. Existing persisted verdicts remain compatible. ## Validation - `npm run transpile-client` - `npm run typecheck-client` - targeted ESLint and repository stylelint for changed Sessions files - `npm run valid-layers-check` - focused comparison tool, orchestration, sidebar, setup, accessibility, and telemetry tests - live Agents window validation with a persisted completed comparison - `git diff --check` Fixes #335085 ## Architecture flow ```mermaid flowchart LR Setup[Choose attempt agents/models
and Judge] -->|Run in parallel| Attempts[Attempts
isolated worktrees] Attempts -->|All terminal| Judge[Judge session
review every diff] Judge -->|1. readAttemptComparison| Evidence[Bounded cross-attempt manifest] Evidence -.->|2. get_session_context
for deeper transcript evidence| Judge Judge -.->|3. targeted tests/build/lint
when evidence is missing| Validation[Validation evidence] Validation --> Judge Judge -->|4. completeAttemptComparison
exactly once| Results[Recommendation
provenance and conflicts] Results -->|Review Recommended Attempt| Review[Attempt session
and Changes editor] Results -->|Optional| Synthesis[Synthesis session] ``` Comparison telemetry records only attempt elapsed time, model configuration, and the Judge selection. Provider-native OTel chat spans supply token consumption for analysis. Neither path records cost or task content. ## Comparison telemetry Comparison telemetry records one elapsed-time event when an attempt's first turn becomes terminal and one model-outcome event after the Judge submits a verdict. Provider-native OTel chat spans carry token usage. The OTel trace anchor and both VS Code events use the same hashed comparison ID and successful-attempt index, so the datasets can be correlated without copying provider token counts into VS Code telemetry. It does **not** include prompts, responses, diffs, file paths, commands, workspace details, validation outcomes, or cost. Provider IDs are reduced to bounded categories (`default-copilot`, `local-agent-host`, `remote-agent-host`, or `other`). | Event | What we log | Why | |---|---|---| | `agents/sessionComparisonAttemptCompleted` | Hashed comparison ID; attempt index; and elapsed milliseconds from session creation until the first turn becomes terminal. | Measure first-turn elapsed time, then join to the model outcome event or provider-native OTel trace by hashed comparison ID and attempt index. | | Provider-native OTel chat spans | `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens` on chat spans in the attempt trace; the trace anchor carries the hashed comparison ID and attempt index. | Analyze token consumption consistently across Copilot, Claude, and Codex without duplicating provider-owned usage into VS Code telemetry. | | `agents/sessionComparisonModelOutcome` | Hashed comparison ID; attempt index and count; bounded provider category, agent ID, and resolved or configured model ID for the attempt; whether the Judge recommended it; and the Judge's bounded provider category, agent ID, and resolved or configured model ID. | Measure which model and harness combinations participate in comparisons and their Judge-selection rate, including how results vary by Judge configuration. | Joining the two VS Code events and the provider-native OTel trace supports aggregate questions such as which models are compared most often, which are selected most often by the Judge, and how first-turn time or token consumption correlates with that selection. Because task content is intentionally omitted, these are directional correlations rather than claims about model quality for a particular task category. ## Judge tools | Tool | What it does | Added for this flow? | |---|---|---| | `readAttemptComparison` | Gives the Judge one bounded manifest of every attempt, worktree, changed file summary, and exact transcript target. | Yes | | `get_session_context` | Lets the Judge inspect one attempt conversation when deeper evidence is needed. | No, reused an existing tool | | standard validation tools | Let the Judge run missing targeted tests, builds, lint, or diagnostics in the attempt worktrees. | No, reused existing tools | | `completeAttemptComparison` | Records one structured recommendation, conflicts, per-attempt findings, validation states, and evidence provenance. | Yes |

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added Set insertion, full-set JSON serialization, startup reload, and absence of pruning in both comparison-removal paths are directly visible in the changed service. Exact profile sizes vary, but the lifetime-linear retention and repeated whole-history serialization do not depend on timing assumptions.
Findings.PerformanceResource: UUID key strings retained in a Set and profile storage, along with repeated full-array/JSON allocations and storage writes.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retained bytes and each save/load cost grow linearly with the lifetime number of completed attempts, including attempts whose comparison was deleted; because the full history is rewritten after each completion, cumulative serialization bytes grow quadratically over continued use.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Unbounded retained memory and profile storage, plus increasing synchronous CPU/GC and storage-write latency after each completed attempt and increasing startup parse cost.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no comparison-attempt telemetry Set or persisted deduplication history, so archived comparison runs left no permanent telemetry-key state and did not add whole-history serialization to session completion.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each completed comparison attempt now permanently adds a UUID-based telemetry-deduplication key to an in-memory Set backed by profile storage, then synchronously serializes the entire accumulated history whenever another attempt completes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added completion path at line 585 inserts `${comparison.id}/${participant.id}` into a profile-lifetime Set, and `_removeComparison`/missing-group cleanup only remove comparison records without deleting the corresponding keys; the added save routine rewrites the full Set after each newly completed attempt.
Findings.Title: Prune completed-attempt telemetry keys with their comparison
Findings.Impact: Users who repeatedly run and archive comparisons accumulate retained strings and an ever-growing profile value. Later attempt completions allocate and serialize the entire history on the session-change critical path, increasing CPU/GC and storage-write latency; window startup also reloads and parses all stale keys.
Findings.Evidence: `_loadAttemptTelemetryState` restores every historical key into `_reportedAttemptTelemetry`; `_captureTerminalAttemptMetrics` adds one key per terminal attempt and calls `_saveAttemptTelemetryState`; that method executes `JSON.stringify([...this._reportedAttemptTelemetry])` and stores it at PROFILE scope. `_removeComparison` and `_removeComparisonsWithMissingGroups` update only `_comparisons`, so archived/deleted comparisons leave these keys resident forever.
Findings.Recommendation: Bound deduplication state to live comparisons: remove and persist all `${comparisonId}/...` keys when a comparison is removed (including missing-group cleanup), or keep/cap the marker within the already bounded comparison record so archived comparisons cannot grow profile state indefinitely.

Scenarios.Scenario: Configure and launch multiple comparison attempts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the user confirms setup, `startComparison` persists the comparison, starts every attempt, and awaits all attempt-launch promises before validating that at least two succeeded. The actual agents then continue in background, so only session/worktree creation and request submission are on the Start action's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a provider-backed agent session, isolated worktree, chat, and initial model request for each attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one provider session creation/send path per configured attempt, with no deduplication even when attempts share a harness; normally 2-4 calls, but the UI has no hard attempt cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR there was no multi-attempt comparison action; users started agent sessions individually rather than fan-out from one action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All launch calls must settle before `startComparison` returns, while the agent executions themselves continue as background sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the current comparison collection and store it in profile storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial full comparison write plus further full-record writes as each attempt reports `onSessionCreated` and final launch state; scales with attempt count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No comparison records or comparison-specific profile writes existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial write is synchronous before launches; participant updates occur during launch callbacks and final reconciliation before completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of attempts the user adds in the setup dialog; effective cardinality is the full attempt count because attempts are deliberately not deduplicated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All configured attempts are started together with `attempts.map(...)` plus `Promise.all`; there is no limiter. This is explicit in the UI ('Start N sessions in parallel'). Typical bakeoffs use 2-4 attempts; larger concurrency is user-created by repeatedly adding attempts.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no launch-result cache or coalescing across configured attempts; each distinct attempt is intentionally independent. Harness/model configuration is resolved before launch, and repeated harness choices still create separate sessions and worktrees.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the Promise.all fan-out, per-attempt provider call, worktree isolation option, and storage writes are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large user-configured attempt counts could create a resource burst, but normal product use and wording center on a small bakeoff; no evidence establishes a regression at realistic 2-4 attempt cardinality, so this intentional parallelism was not reported.
Scenarios.Verdict: Intentional, visible parallelism with potentially high fan-out but no concrete realistic regression beyond the feature's required cost; no finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Launch the Judge and optional synthesis after attempts finish
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Judge launch is gated until all attempts are terminal and at least two completed. It then creates one Judge session; synthesis similarly creates at most one session after a verdict/user plan. These agent runs are necessarily on the comparison-result critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create an isolated provider session/worktree and send the Judge or synthesis request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider-backed Judge session per eligible comparison, then zero or one synthesis session if requested/configured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These comparison-only agent sessions did not exist before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Judge model request must finish before a verdict can be displayed; synthesis must finish before its implementation is available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One comparison with its attempt count; Judge and synthesis creation remain O(1), while their prompts/manifests scale with the attempt count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one Judge and one synthesis participant per comparison; guards and persisted participant roles prevent concurrent duplicate launches. The Agent Host fallback handles a disconnected-client case, not an additional normal launch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The comparison record and participant resources are retained in memory/profile storage. `_judgeStarting` and the presence of a Judge participant suppress duplicate launches in the window; Agent Host launch state is reconstructed from in-memory session summaries rather than cached separately.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: terminal-state gating, launch guards, and the single provider creation calls are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider duration and worktree cost vary, but launch cardinality is tightly bounded per comparison.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable scheduling regression: the expensive boundaries are required, occur once per role, and duplicate launch is guarded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Read the bounded comparison manifest for judging or synthesis
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A Judge or synthesis agent invokes the tool once before evaluating attempts. Building and serializing the manifest is on that tool call's critical path, but no subprocess, filesystem scan, network request, or transcript IPC is performed by the changed tool itself.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assemble and JSON-serialize a bounded comparison manifest from in-memory session state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One JSON serialization per invocation, containing each launched attempt and at most 200 changed-file entries per attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No comparison manifest was produced before this feature.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization must complete before the Judge/synthesis agent receives evidence.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of launched attempts times up to 200 changed-file summaries per attempt, after excluding participants without session resources.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One synchronous in-memory assembly/serialization per tool invocation; prompts direct the agent to call it exactly once.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The tool reads already-maintained session metadata and changed-file observables; it does not load full transcripts. There is no manifest cache because the result must reflect current lifecycle/verdict data.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the slice bound and single JSON.stringify call are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Attempt count is user-configurable, but per-attempt changed-file content is capped at 200 and normal attempt counts are small.
Scenarios.Verdict: Serialization is deliberately bounded per attempt and called once in the intended flow; no performance finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open comparison participants in a tiled session grid
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Open in Grid action resolves, checks, and prepares every selected participant session before committing the grid layout. These awaits are sequential, so all preparation is on the UI action's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve each session and optionally ask its provider to prepare it for opening.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolve/can-open/optional provider-prepare chain per selected unique session, normally the 2-4 attempts plus optionally Judge/synthesis.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Before the PR sessions were opened individually; there was no comparison bulk-grid action placing all selected sessions behind one launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Every chain completes before any grid layout is shown.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct participant session resources selected for the grid after ResourceMap deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Session resolution and provider preparation are serialized in a loop; layout restoration is a single synchronous transaction after all unique sessions are ready.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A `ResourceMap` deduplicates sessions after resolution. Provider preparation may exploit provider-internal warm state, but this method has no explicit cache; already-materialized session objects avoid rediscovery.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for sequential critical-path placement; variable for actual provider cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Some providers make preparation a no-op while restored/remote sessions can be slower. Realistic comparison cardinality is small, and ordering/cancellation semantics may require serialization.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence finding: the method serializes provider preparation, but realistic cardinality is small and evidence does not establish materially worse user-visible latency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render ordinary session rows and chat views, including when comparisons are unused
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating a Sessions list template now synchronously creates hidden comparison status controls, buttons, hover registrations, and listeners; constructing any ChatView creates the hidden comparison-result component and markdown renderer. Layout also updates the hidden result node. All occur on normal non-comparison rendering paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously materialized session row/group templates and live ChatView panes, not total stored sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI thread; work is synchronous during template/view construction and layout. Tree recycling bounds concurrent row-template count to the viewport/overscan population.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session tree virtualizes and recycles row/group templates, so new comparison DOM and listeners scale with rendered templates rather than total history. `SessionComparisonResult` is retained per live ChatView and reuses its node/renderer across session changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for eager synchronous allocation; low for material user-visible magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The eager work is real and applies even with the experiment disabled, but virtualized cardinality is low and the added objects/listeners are lightweight enough that no concrete dropped-frame or meaningful startup-latency impact is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: Candidate eager-work pattern inspected and rejected as a finding because virtualization/reuse bounds row cost and evidence does not show a material regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Persist comparison state and deduplicate completed-attempt telemetry across restarts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On window/service initialization, the entire stored array is synchronously read and parsed into the Set. When a terminal attempt first gains elapsed time, telemetry capture adds its key and synchronously serializes/stores the full Set on the session-change path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load or rewrite the complete profile-lifetime array of telemetry deduplication keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One profile read/JSON parse at service initialization; then up to one full-history profile write per terminal-completion event batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No comparison telemetry-key profile entry, startup parse, or completion write existed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Startup parse/load blocks service construction; completion serialization and storage execute synchronously inside session-change processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copy the Set to an array and stringify the entire accumulated key history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-array allocation and JSON serialization per event batch that observes at least one previously unreported completed attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No whole-history comparison telemetry serialization occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs before the session-change callback returns and grows with all historical attempts, not current comparisons.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Lifetime number of completed attempts across all comparisons, including comparisons later archived or deleted; effective save count is terminal event batches after cache misses.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A session-change callback checks retained comparisons synchronously. Multiple newly observed completions within one comparison check coalesce to one save, but completions arriving in separate provider events each trigger another whole-Set save.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The persisted Set acts as a positive deduplication cache for telemetry, so warm checks avoid duplicate telemetry events. However it reloads every historical key at startup and has no eviction when a comparison/group is removed, making warm-state cost grow for the profile lifetime.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: insertion, persisted reload/full save, and both removal paths were traced directly; neither cleanup path deletes keys.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact time to reach thousands of attempts depends on feature adoption and usage, but the absence of pruning makes lifetime-linear retention and repeated O(history) work certain for continuing users.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable unbounded-retention regression; submitted a medium-severity finding anchored to the Set insertion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stop, clean up, or archive all comparison participants
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Stop All waits for every active cancellation in parallel. Startup cleanup waits for parallel cancellations and then parallel deletions. Archive Comparison awaits provider archive operations sequentially before deleting the group.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel active agent requests and delete their provider sessions/worktrees.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cancellation model load/IPC per active participant, then one provider deletion per participant during failed/orphaned startup cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no comparison-wide cleanup path; individual session actions performed the equivalent per session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The respective cleanup phase waits for all calls; cancellation and deletion phases are ordered, while calls within each phase are parallel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Archive each comparison participant through its sessions provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider archive call per comparison group member.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Users could invoke existing multi-session/group archive actions, which also await archive operations sequentially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Calls are sequential and the group is deleted only after all archive operations finish.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active/all participant sessions after filtering active statuses; normally attempts plus at most Judge and synthesis.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cancellation and deletion are `Promise.allSettled` fan-outs; archive calls are serialized, matching existing multi-session archive actions elsewhere in the repository.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cancellation acquires/loads chat models as needed and disposes references afterward. There is no comparison-level result cache; session/provider state remains authoritative.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cardinality and concurrency structure.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider cancellation/archive latency varies, but comparisons normally contain a small participant set.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance regression: parallel cleanup bounds latency, and sequential archive follows existing group-action behavior at small cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all changed files and traced launch, Judge/synthesis, manifest, grid, UI, persistence, and cleanup paths. Submitted one finding for profile-lifetime telemetry-key retention and repeated whole-history serialization. Other fan-out, sequential preparation, and eager UI candidates were bounded, intentional, or lacked evidence of material impact.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
